historicalReferences: Watkins Glen has seen its fair share of drama over the years. Think back to 1973, when Francois Cevert tragically lost his life here, a dark day in motorsport history.
Mario Andretti secured his first Formula 1 victory here in 1978, a momentous occasion for American motorsport.
The Can-Am series was a regular fixture at Watkins Glen, showcasing some of the most powerful and innovative racing cars of all time.
Watkins Glen hosted the US Grand Prix for two decades, from 1961 to 1980, becoming a cornerstone of the Formula 1 calendar.
The 1975 US Grand Prix saw Niki Lauda clinch his first World Championship title. A day etched in motorsport history.
Who could forget the battles between James Hunt and Mario Andretti in the late 70s? Watkins Glen was often the scene of their epic duels.
In recent years, IndyCar has returned to Watkins Glen, providing thrilling racing and spectacular overtakes.
Watkins Glen has been a proving ground for generations of American drivers. It's a track that demands respect and rewards bravery.
The Six Hours of The Glen is a legendary endurance race, testing the limits of both car and driver.
Let's not forget the Trans-Am series, which has a long and storied history at Watkins Glen.
cornerCallouts: The run down to Turn 1 is crucial here, drivers jostling for position before the tight right-hander.
Through the Esses, a true test of car balance and driver skill, requiring pinpoint accuracy.
Onto the back straight, a prime overtaking opportunity with the benefit of DRS.
Braking hard for the Bus Stop chicane, it's easy to lock up and lose valuable time.
Negotiating the Carousel, a long, sweeping left-hander that puts immense strain on the tires.
Coming out of the Carousel, drivers need to get on the power early to maximize their speed onto the short straight.
The Outer Loop is a high-speed section that demands commitment and precision.
The final corner, Turn 9, is a challenging right-hander that leads onto the pit straight. Getting a good exit here is vital for a strong lap time.
strategyPoints: Tire wear will be a major factor in today's race. The abrasive surface of Watkins Glen takes its toll, especially on the left-front tire.
The pit window is relatively short here, around 22 seconds. Teams will need to execute their stops flawlessly to avoid losing track position.
Fuel consumption is also a concern, particularly in the early stages of the race when the cars are heavy with fuel.
With the long straights and high-speed corners, aerodynamic efficiency is key. Teams will be looking for the optimal balance between downforce and drag.
The Boot configuration offers limited overtaking opportunities, so track position is crucial. A good start and a well-timed pit stop can make all the difference.
Safety cars are common at Watkins Glen. Teams need to be prepared to react quickly to changing race conditions.
Managing tire temperatures is vital, especially in the cooler conditions. Drivers will need to be careful not to overheat their tires early in the stint.
The relatively short lap length of 4.5 km means that traffic will be a constant factor throughout the race.
